# READOUT: uniform control (a1) is the BEST; every per-type LR intervention is WORSE at this fork/horizon.
# - The predicted-best arm (a5 polar) is the WORST (+0.024). The per-type rule (a2) does NOT beat control (+0.0024), contradicting the expected "a2 beats a1 by 0.001-0.006".

# - Rule-direction signal exists but is net-harmful: a2 (rule, 3.51295) < a4 (anti-rule, 3.51515) by 0.0022, so equalizing curvature helps vs anti-equalizing -- but BOTH are worse than doing nothing (uniform LR).

# - Mechanism-death test ("if a4 also beats control"): a4 does NOT beat control (it is worse), so that specific condition is not met; but neither does a2, so the design provides no net gain over uniform LR here.
# n=1/arm; the >=0.002 gaps are ~10x the ~2e-4 val seed-noise floor (REQ-027), so control-beats-all is robust; a2-vs-a4 (0.0022) is real but small.
